subject: Stonebridge: reserved throughput shortfall and immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Stonebridge throughput alert: reserved capacity shortfall

Team —

Monitoring just surfaced a serious runtime signal for Stonebridge (SB-202611). Key points from the alert: 
- Reserved throughput fully saturated across the east-us dedicated pool serving their tenant (100% commit hit).
- P95 latency up ~3.2x vs baseline for their production route; tail 99th has noticeable spikes.
- 5xx rate climbed from ~0.02% to 1.6% over last 30m; token queueing visible in the inference pipeline.

I pulled the metrics snapshot (attached: stonebridge_metrics_11_18.csv). Immediate asks: 
1) Marissa / Naomi: quick triage — is this noisy-neighbor (other tenant spill) or a workload change on Stonebridge's side? Tell me the root-suspects in the next 15 min.
2) David: can we authorize a temporary fallback to the compatible smaller model variant + enable autoscale burst for the pool? If there are cost/contract implications we need a quick cost estimate.
3) I want a short customer note (apology + tactical mitigations) ready at 08:55 so we can sync with them at 09:00.

We need to move fast — Stonebridge is a priority account and this is hitting end users.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stonebridge throughput alert: reserved capacity shortfall

Alex — quick update after an initial ops sweep: 
- This looks like a behavioral change in the customer workload rather than noisy neighbor. Their token distribution shifted (longer contexts) after last night's feature release; KV cache churn increased and sequence lengths spiked. That pushes per-request token work up and reduces effective throughput on the reserved pool.
- Dedicated pool metrics show sustained POOL_UTIL > 95% for the last 40 minutes; queue depth is climbing. No obvious OOMs but retry storms from client-side timeouts are feeding back into retries.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (in order of impact):
1) Serve a compatible, lower-throughput model variant for their prod route (drop from gptx-large -> gptx-medium) — minimal quality regression but halves token cost and frees headroom.
2) Enable short-lived burst capacity for the pool (2 hours) to relieve the immediate queueing while we flatten the spike. Procurement/exec sign-off needed for the burst cost.
3) Apply conservative rate-limiting on non-critical endpoints and enable KV prefix caching for repeat prefixes (we can push config in 20–30m).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (draft MAP for customer-facing timeline).

I can have a technical postmortem checklist and short customer wording in the next 25 minutes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@stonebridge.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@stonebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, procurement@stonebridge.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Stonebridge production impact — immediate mitigations and next steps

Rajesh / Lisa —

First, I want to apologize for the degradation you are seeing this morning. We're treating this as highest priority. Summary: we've observed your reserved throughput reach capacity and that is causing increased latency and intermittent 5xx errors on your production endpoints.

What we're doing now (immediate):
- Rolling a compatible model fallback (gptx-medium) for your production route to reduce per-request token work. This should reduce tail latency within ~10–15 minutes.
- Preparing a short burst authorization to add temporary capacity while we stabilize.
- Applying conservative rate limits to non-critical internal routes to preserve headroom for production traffic.

Attached is a short mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_v2.docx) with proposed timeline. Can we do a 20–25m huddle at 09:30 PST to confirm the rollback and burst? If you prefer, we can trigger the rollback now — I need a quick confirm from you to proceed immediately.

Thank you and sorry again for the disruption — we will keep you posted every 15 minutes.

Alex Martinez

From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@stonebridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@stonebridge.com>, procurement@stonebridge.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Stonebridge production impact — immediate mitigations and next steps

Alex — thanks for the note but this is unacceptable for our production users. We're seeing customer-facing errors and support tickets spike. A few points: 
- We did push a release last night, but it was within the agreed throughput profile. Your platform should absorb transient shifts; this is why we pay for reserved throughput.
- We need an immediate SLA fallback and formal credit for the period our customers were impacted. Please escalate to your leadership — I want a conversation with an exec (CTO or Head of Customer Ops) within the hour.

If you can enact the rollback immediately that's good, but we will expect prompt follow-up on credits and a full root-cause analysis. Procurement is copied.

- Rajesh
Head of Engineering
Stonebridge Financial

Subject: Escalation: Stonebridge exec ask and authorization request

Vivek / David — quick exec summary and asks (for your visibility/action):

What happened: Stonebridge is experiencing a reserved-capacity throughput shortfall driven by a workload change (longer contexts / KV churn). This produced elevated latencies and increased 5xxs for a ~50k active QPS window on their tenant routes.

Immediate asks for execs: 
1) Approve a two-hour burst authorization (estimated cost $35k–$50k) so we can relieve the pool and avoid further customer-visible errors. We need sign-off now to flip the burst.
2) Authorize a one-time customer credit (preliminary ask from customer) — recommend we offer a goodwill credit and commit to a joint post-mortem. Please advise level of credit we can approve at the AC level.
3) Approve temporary downgrade to gptx-medium for their prod route (ops already queued the change).

Suggested next steps: Vivek, can you join the 09:30 PST (now 10:04) bridge if we need to talk with Stonebridge execs? David, please confirm whether procurement constraints block immediate burst activation and route any procurement approvals to me.

Links: Jira SB-2345 (incident), MAP draft (Drive link).

I will prepare a concise 1-pager for the CEO/COO if you want a readout. I'll keep the customer and Marissa looped on status.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
